chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Abd al-Rahman ibnman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Minhal al-Qassab, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not receive [goods] outside the city, for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) forbade the receiving [of goods outside the city].' I said: 'And what is the limit of the receiving?' He said: 'What is less than a Gadwa or a Rawha.' I said: 'And how much is the Gadwa and the Rawha?' He said: 'Four Farsakhs.'
Ibn Abi Umeyr said: 'And what is above that, so it is not (classified as) receiving [outside the city].'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.التَّلَقِّي: Receiving goods from traders outside the city before they enter the market
key_terms.رَوْحَةٌ: An afternoon journey, used here as a unit of distance
key_terms.غَدْوَةٌ: A morning journey, used here as a unit of distance
key_terms.فَرَاسِخَ: Farsakhs, a unit of distance (plural of Farsakh)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on buying goods directly from traders outside the city limits?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi delineates the specific geographic boundary for 'Talaqqi al-Rukban' (pre-market buying), defining the prohibited zone as within four Farsakhs (approximately six miles) from the city limits. It reflects the Prophetic practice of preventing middlemen from monopolizing goods and inflating prices before they reach the main market, a principle upheld in Shia jurisprudence to ensure fair trade practices.
